approach: Fix the class where it starts: the listing and settling of dispatched jobs that have no process. `steward::interrupted_work` drops a dispatched job in four ways. (1) It keeps only the `cli` and `steward` channels (steward.rs:467). (2) It hides every job that any later request retries, whatever became of that retry (steward.rs:448-460), while `athena status` uses `retries_by_job`, where a dropped retry does not stand (reading/retry.rs:246-267). (3) Nothing closes the original once its retry ends, so status shows it as "retried as X" for ever. (4) `Drain::prepare` skips reading interrupted items (drain.rs:2132) but still passes their old plan entry to `Plan::build_improving`, which refuses an incomplete entry. The change: (a) `interrupted_work` drops the channel filter and excludes jobs that `retries_by_job` says a retry stands for. (b) A new pure `steward::settle_interrupted(records, running)` returns Close(reason) or Hold(reason) per dispatched job with no process. (c) A new defaulted `Steps::settle_interrupted` hook; `RealSteps` implements it with the existing `Athena::close`. Drain calls it before `queue()` and after `sweep`, and notes every line. (d) `prepare` removes the incomplete plan entry of an interrupted item so its retry re-reads the request. status.rs is not edited, since it already lists every dispatched job with no process; tests pin that. hestia.rs is NOT edited (revision finding 3): the settle reason starts with the literal `re-queued as `, the same text hestia itself writes (hestia.rs:2409) and tests for (hestia.rs:342-354); a steward unit test pins the literal. The six live jobs get operator commands against the live records, outside the diff.

decisions.choice: Fix the class in `steward::interrupted_work` plus a new pure `steward::settle_interrupted`, called from drain through a defaulted `Steps` hook.
decisions.reason: One listing function causes the gap, so fixing it covers every job, not six. A defaulted trait method leaves the many test stubs (tests/drain.rs Stub, Unaccepted, Replay, WithRealCheck, Shared, Rebasing; drain.rs test steps) unedited, as `reclaim_interrupted` does (drain.rs:576). The decision logic is a pure function over `Records`, unit-tested without a model.

rejected.why: `queue()` is also used by `athena plan`, which must stay read-only; closing there hides a side effect.
Forces edits to every stub and widens the diff.

decisions.choice: Drop the channel filter for interrupted jobs only; keep `DRAINED_CHANNELS` for `queued_work` (steward.rs:414).
decisions.reason: A queued request on another channel may belong to another consumer that will start it. A dispatched job with no registry process belongs to nobody. The existing test at tests/drain.rs:5122 asserts the opposite and is rewritten.

rejected.option: Remove the channel filter from `queued_work` too
rejected.why: Changes unrelated queued-request behavior; the brief says not to change unrelated stages.

rejected.option: Keep the filter and only close off-channel jobs with a reason
rejected.why: Discards resumable work; resuming is the first choice.

decisions.choice: Close with the existing `Athena::close` (abandoned outcome with a stated reason). The reason for a job whose retry ended is `re-queued as <retry>, which ended <state>`, built from a private literal prefix `re-queued as ` in steward.rs. hestia.rs is not edited.
decisions.reason: `close` already recovers invocation records, scores, cleans the job and commits under the gate, so no new record or schema is added. Hestia's `closed_by_person` (hestia.rs:346-354) treats an abandoned job whose reason lacks the `re-queued as ` prefix as a person's close and skips the cause; a system settle must not look like a person's. Using the same literal text keeps that rule true without widening scope to hestia.rs (the constant is private there, hestia.rs:342). A steward unit test pins the literal prefix; hestia already writes the same text at hestia.rs:2409.

rejected.option: Make `REQUEUE_CLOSE_REASON` `pub(crate)` in hestia.rs and share it
rejected.why: hestia.rs is not a listed deliverable; the finding says it widens scope. The shared text is a one-line literal pinned by a test.

rejected.option: A new OutcomeState or record kind
rejected.why: Touches athena-data, the gate and round-trip tests for no gain.
Bypasses the gate; hand-written job records are detected (commit d1358ed).

decisions.choice: Settle follows a chain of retries that are themselves interrupted and closes them together in one pass, with a depth cap.
decisions.reason: `retries_by_job` treats an abandoned retry as not standing (retry.rs:253-262). Closing only the middle job of Z, A (retry of Z), B (retry of A, landed) would make Z reappear unretried and be retried again.

decisions.choice: Exempt interrupted items with an incomplete plan entry from the plan (remove their entry in `prepare`) instead of refusing them.
decisions.reason: Their first attempt is `athena retry`, which re-reads the request (drain.rs:1860), so the old reading's plan fields are irrelevant; `prepare` never reads them to fill the gap (drain.rs:2132).

rejected.option: Read interrupted items in `prepare` to fill the plan
rejected.why: Spends a model call on a job the retry reads again anyway.

decisions.choice: Leave status.rs unchanged and pin its behavior with tests.
decisions.reason: `state_name` marks every dispatched job with no registry process as `interrupted`, and `scan_jobs` (status.rs:889-948, 962-976) puts it in `open` for every channel with an `athena retry` or `retried as` next line. risks.risk: Closing an original too early could lose work, or retry it twice.
risks.mitigation: Settle closes only when the standing retry (followed through interrupted retries) has an outcome, or the job has no request record. An open retry gives a Hold note, no close. Unit tests cover running, open, closed and chained cases; a drain test asserts the retried original is not retried twice.

risks.risk: `retries_by_job` treats an abandoned retry as not standing, so closing a middle job could re-list its parent for a second retry.
risks.mitigation: `settle_interrupted` follows the chain and closes every interrupted job in it in one pass, with a depth cap like `MAX_RETRY_DEPTH`. A unit test covers Z-A-B.

risks.risk: Hestia would read a settle close as a person's and skip the cause, since the prefix text is now duplicated, not shared (hestia.rs is not edited).
risks.mitigation: The reason starts with the literal `re-queued as `, the same text hestia writes at hestia.rs:2409. The steward test `settle_reason_starts_with_the_requeue_prefix` pins it, and the producer must not change hestia.rs.

risks.risk: Resuming off-channel jobs reverses a documented rule and an existing test.
risks.mitigation: The rewrite is explicit and called out in the CHANGELOG. `queued_work` keeps its channel filter, pinned by a new test. The change applies only to dispatched jobs with no registry process.

risks.risk: Closing during a parallel drain could race with a worker.
risks.mitigation: Settle errors become notes and never fail the drain. `close` takes the job lock and refuses a job another process runs. The final call comes after all workers finish (after `sweep`).

risks.risk: The `interrupt` helper might leave an invocation record, so the fixture would not show 'stopped before the producer'.
risks.mitigation: Each test asserts the job has no invocation and no outcome before the drain; the producer reads lifecycle.rs 1309-1320 first. If the shapes cannot be separated, use the low-disk hold before the producer (`go_with_disk`, tests/drain.rs:2424), which leaves the job dispatched with no candidate.

risks.risk: The actual cause for the six live jobs may be one of the four paths and not the others.
risks.mitigation: Each path has its own test, so a wrong guess on one leaves none untested. The real cause is named in open_questions as a host fact.

risks.risk: The six outcomes cannot be written by the diff because records/ is excluded.
risks.mitigation: The diff contains only code, tests and CHANGELOG. Demonstration 4 is an operator step after merge, each close citing a hash found by reading the job's brief and git log.

risks.risk: The expected-deliverables list names status.rs, run/mod.rs, reading/retry.rs, which this plan does not edit.
risks.mitigation: Not editing them is safe: status.rs already lists every dispatched job, `retries_by_job` is reused unchanged, run/mod.rs is unrelated to the fault. If the producer finds a reason to touch them, it says why in the CHANGELOG entry.
